item.title: WATCH | Dr Aamira Vally of the ARC gives tips on biosecurity
item.description: The virus that causes foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) can survive for up to six months in certain types of material, which must be taken into account by farmers when taking biosecurity measures. This was the advice of Dr Aamira Vally, a veterinarian with the Agricultural Research Council Irene Animal Production, at a cattle farmers’ day at Dr Pieter de Kock’s farm near Thabazimbi.

item.title: Land reform gets second chance: WIPHOLD’s plan to resurrect Zebediela Citrus Farm
item.description: After years of uncertainty and decline, the Limpopo government has secured what it believes is the right strategic partner to restore the historic Zebediela Citrus Estate to its former glory.

item.title: Treasury under pressure as Ramaphosa targets child malnutrition
item.description: President Cyril Ramaphosa has committed South Africa to ending child stunting by 2030, placing child nutrition firmly on the national agenda. The announcement, made during the State of the Nation Address (SONA) on 12 February, followed Cabinet’s approval of the National Strategy to Accelerate Action for Children (NSAAC), which outlines 10 priorities to improve the lives of children and teenagers.

item.title: FMD awareness | How foot-and-mouth disease spreads
item.description: Foot-and-mouth disease spreads quickly and easily – but understanding how the virus moves is the first step in protecting your livestock. Here’s what every farmer and livestock owner needs to know.

item.title: Trust the numbers, not tradition, when making farming decisions
item.description: Dirk Lesch produces wheat, canola and wine grapes on the farm Elim near Malmesbury in the Western Cape. He does his bookkeeping himself, he says; it gives him a good overview of his business and ensures every cent is accounted for.

item.title: FMD | Claims that farmers must pay or register for vaccines are false
item.description: Individuals or companies that tell farmers they must pay upfront to obtain vaccines, or register on specific systems to qualify for them, are spreading “absolute nonsense”, according to the FMD Industry Coordination Council.

item.title: WATCH | Boerbok and Meatmaster mastery in Limpopo
item.description: African Farming recently travelled to Limpopo to meet Nicholus Kutama Huma, who farms side by side with his father, Israel Huma, with Boerbok goats and Meatmaster sheep in the Makgabeng village outside Bochum in the Blouberg Local Municipality.

item.title: Good demand for Johanri Dormers
item.description: Demand for Dormer ewes, both commercial and stud, was particularly strong at the Johanri production auction of Johan and Anri Barnard on the farm Spioenkop near Lindley, Free State. Particularly high average prices, especially for the commercial ewes, were achieved.

item.title: FMD | Vaccination update from Gauteng
item.description: The Gauteng Department of Agriculture and Rural Development began administering its allocated share – 70 000 doses – of the first consignment of foot-and-mouth disease vaccine from Argentina on Thursday, 26 February.
